config.title: list-style and counters

intro.title: list-style and counters
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a styled, multi-level list—like a nested to-do list or a document outline—to visually organize information. You will learn the core CSS concepts of list-style and counters, which control the appearance of list items and enable automatic numbering across complex structures. The main technologies involved are CSS properties such as list-style-type, list-style-position, list-style-image, and the counter-reset, counter-increment, and content functions with the counter() value. By the end, you'll be able to customize bullet points, adjust their positioning, and create custom, automated numbering sequences for your web content.
intro.usecase: The `list-style` and `counter` properties are essential for creating structured, readable content in real-world applications. Developers use them to style navigation menus, table of contents, and step-by-step instructions in dashboards or documentation sites. For example, an e-commerce admin panel might use custom counters to number order items or a blog platform could apply unique bullet styles to category lists. Mastering these properties allows you to build polished, user-friendly interfaces that enhance content hierarchy and visual consistency.

objectives: Apply the list-style shorthand to configure bullet appearance, position, and image for unordered lists.
Implement custom counter-reset and counter-increment properties to create sequential numbering for ordered lists.
Construct a multi-level nested list with distinct list-style types at each level.
Manipulate counter values to display custom formats using the content property with counters.
Integrate list-style-image to replace default bullets with custom graphics.
Control the visual spacing and alignment of list items using list-style-position.
Initialize and render a custom counter that resets at specific container elements.

steps.title: Create HTML structure for list demonstration
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with a basic structure including an ordered list and an unordered list that will be targeted by CSS.
steps.hint: Start with the <!DOCTYPE html> declaration, then add <html>, <head>, and <body> tags. Inside the body, create one <ol> with three <li> items and one <ul> with three <li> items.
steps.analogousExample:
1. First ordered item
  2. Second ordered item
  3. Third ordered item
  • First unordered item
  • Second unordered item
  • Third unordered item
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>List Demo</title>
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add ordered list here -->
    <!-- Add unordered list here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: A complete HTML file with both ordered and unordered lists containing three items each, ready for CSS styling.
successCriteria: The HTML file contains both an <ol> and a <ul>, each with three <li> elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both an ordered list (<ol>) and an unordered list (<ul>), each with three list items (<li>).
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a complete HTML file with both an ordered list and an unordered list, each containing three items. Check that you have the correct HTML structure with <!DOCTYPE html>, <html>, <head>, and <body> tags.

steps.title: Link CSS file and create basic list styling
steps.instruction: In the HTML head section, add a link element to connect a CSS file named 'styles.css'.
steps.hint: Use <link rel='stylesheet' href='styles.css'> inside the <head> tags. In the CSS file, write li { } to target list items.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>List Demo</title>
    <!-- Add link to CSS file here -->
</head>
<body>
    <!-- Add ordered list here -->
    <!-- Add unordered list here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The HTML file will have a link to 'styles.css' in the head, and the CSS file will contain a rule targeting list items.
successCriteria: A link element with rel='stylesheet' and href='styles.css' is added to the head, and a CSS file named 'styles.css' exists with a li selector rule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've added both the link element in HTML and the li rule in the CSS file.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the link element correctly in the head and created a CSS file with a li selector.

steps.title: create that CSS file and add a rule to target
steps.instruction: create that CSS file and add a rule to target all list items with basic styling.
steps.hint: Use <link rel='stylesheet' href='styles.css'> inside the <head> tags. In the CSS file, write li { } to target list items.
steps.seedCode:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>

    <!-- Add link to CSS file here -->
</head>

steps.feedbackPartial: Review the instruction and try again.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction and try again.

steps.title: Apply list-style-type to unordered lists
steps.instruction: In your CSS file, add a rule for unordered lists that sets the list-style-type property to 'square'.
steps.hint: Use the ul selector followed by curly braces, then write list-style-type: square; inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: The unordered list bullets will change from default discs to squares.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a rule for ul with list-style-type set to 'square'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're targeting unordered lists with 'ul' and setting list-style-type to 'square'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't seem right. Check if you used the correct selector and property.

steps.title: Apply list-style-type to ordered lists
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule that targets ordered lists (<ol>) and sets list-style-type to 'decimal'.
steps.hint: Use the 'ol' selector and the 'list-style-type' property with the value 'decimal'.
steps.expectedOutcome: Ordered lists will display with standard decimal numbers (1, 2, 3, etc.).
successCriteria: The CSS contains a rule for 'ol' with 'list-style-type: decimal'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've applied decimal numbering to ordered lists.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're targeting 'ol' and setting 'list-style-type' to 'decimal'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Try using 'ol { list-style-type: decimal; }'.

steps.title: Use list-style-position property
steps.instruction: Add the list-style-position property to your unordered list selector and set it to 'inside'.
steps.hint: The list-style-position property controls whether list markers (bullets/numbers) appear inside or outside the content flow. Use 'inside' to make bullets appear within the list item's content box.
steps.expectedOutcome: The unordered list bullets will now appear inside the content area of each list item, affecting the text indentation.
successCriteria: The unordered list selector includes list-style-position: inside;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added list-style-position: inside to the unordered list selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The list-style-position property wasn't correctly applied. Check that you've added it to the ul selector with the value 'inside'.

steps.title: Apply list-style-image for custom markers
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the unordered list to use a custom image as the list marker with the list-style-image property. Use the URL 'https://example.com/star.png' as the image source.
steps.hint: The list-style-image property accepts a URL to an image. You can add this property to the existing ul selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The unordered list will display custom star images instead of the default square bullets.
successCriteria: The unordered list selector includes the list-style-image property with the URL 'https://example.com/star.png'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the list-style-image property with the correct URL value to the ul selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The list-style-image property is missing or incorrect. Check that you've added it to the ul selector with the URL 'https://example.com/star.png'.

steps.title: Use list-style shorthand property
steps.instruction: In the CSS file, apply the list-style shorthand property to the unordered list (ul) to combine the type, position, and image properties in a single declaration.
steps.hint: The list-style shorthand property accepts values for list-style-type, list-style-position, and list-style-image in any order. Use the values already defined in the ul selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: The unordered list will now use the shorthand list-style property, combining the previously defined type and position values.
successCriteria: The ul selector uses the list-style shorthand property with appropriate values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the shorthand property might be missing a value or have incorrect syntax. Check the order and values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The list-style shorthand property was not applied correctly. Review the syntax and ensure you're combining the type, position, and image values.

steps.title: Initialize CSS counter with counter-reset
steps.instruction: Initialize a CSS counter named 'section' on the ordered list container using the counter-reset property.
steps.hint: Add a counter-reset property to the ol selector and set its value to 'section'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ordered list container will have a CSS counter named 'section' ready for use in later steps.
successCriteria: The ol selector includes a counter-reset property with the value 'section'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added counter-reset: section; to the ol selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The counter wasn't initialized correctly. Check that you've added counter-reset: section; to the ol selector.

steps.title: Increment counters with counter-increment
steps.instruction: Add the counter-increment property to the ordered list items to increase the counter value for each list item.
steps.hint: Use the counter-increment property with the counter name you defined earlier (e.g., 'myCounter').
steps.expectedOutcome: The ordered list items will now increment the counter value with each item.
successCriteria: The counter-increment property is applied to list items with the correct counter name.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the counter-increment property is correctly applied to list items with the counter name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The counter-increment property is missing or incorrect. Ensure you add it to list items with the correct counter name.

steps.title: Display counters with content and counter() function
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for the ::before pseudo-element on ordered list items to display the counter value using the content property and counter() function.
steps.hint: Use the selector 'ol li::before' and set content: counter(chapter) with a separator like '.' and a space.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ordered list items will show custom counter numbers (like "1.", "2.", etc.) before each item.
successCriteria: The CSS includes a rule for 'ol li::before' with 'content: counter(chapter) ". "'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct selector and the content property with counter(chapter).
steps.feedbackWrong: The rule for displaying counter values is missing or incorrect. Check the selector and content property syntax.

steps.title: Create nested counters with counter-reset and counter-increment
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for nested ordered lists (ol ol) that resets a new counter named 'subcounter' and increments it for each list item.
steps.hint: Use the selector 'ol ol' to target nested ordered lists. Inside the rule, set 'counter-reset: subcounter;' and 'counter-increment: subcounter;'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS file will include a rule for nested ordered lists that initializes and increments a separate counter for hierarchical numbering.
successCriteria: A CSS rule with selector 'ol ol' is added, containing both 'counter-reset: subcounter;' and 'counter-increment: subcounter;' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your rule targets 'ol ol' and includes both 'counter-reset: subcounter;' and 'counter-increment: subcounter;' properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The nested counter rule isn't set up correctly. Check that you're using the right selector and including both counter properties.

steps.title: Combine list-style and counters in a practical example
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS rule for a custom ordered list class that combines list-style properties with CSS counters for custom numbering.
steps.hint: Define a class selector like .custom-list, then apply both list-style properties (like list-style-type or list-style-image) and counter properties (counter-reset, counter-increment, and content with counter()) together.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule will be added that demonstrates how to style a list with custom markers while using CSS counters for custom numbering.
successCriteria: A new CSS class selector is created with at least one list-style property and at least one counter property (counter-reset, counter-increment, or content with counter()).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the rule, but make sure it includes both list-style properties (like list-style-type) and counter properties (like counter-reset or counter-increment).
steps.feedbackWrong: The rule doesn't combine list-style and counter properties. Try creating a class selector and adding both types of properties to it.
